BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$17.4 billion, or -17%, in July, to -$118.8 billion, the largest gap since March 2025.

US goods imports rose +$11.4 billion, or +4%, to $318.2 billion, their highest level since March 2025.

Capital goods imports, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors and telecommunications equipment, surged +11%, their largest monthly increase since 1993.

At the same time, exports fell -$6.0 billion, or -3%, to $199.4 billion, their lowest since January, driven by a -11% decline in exports of industrial goods.

Excluding the 4 months between December 2024 and March 2025, when companies accelerated imports ahead of anticipated US tariff increases, July’s goods trade deficit was the largest on record.

The trade gap is widening again.

The rest of the world can hardly tolerate another sustained period of dollar strength.

The suppression of yields and a structurally weaker dollar are likely to be two of the defining macro forces of this decade.

The way I think about my analysis, is it's not focused on traders although they can certainly use it for that. Instead, the idea is that most of us have Bitcoin as a core part of our life savings. It's also volatile, which means our life savings is volatile.

My analysis is aimed at helping HODLers better understand and visualise WHY Bitcoin moves the way it does. This calms the nerves and educates along the way.

Same reason athletes still have personal trainers, you always benefit from someone who is a professional adding fresh perspective. You also needle to keep going to the gym to maintain results.
